hypotheses.hypothesis: N, S and D source surfaces can lower to one deterministic typed RelationId IR without changing relation identity.
support: 17/17 matched current relation specimens lowered to the same typed relation tuples in each local arm
whitespace variants preserved canonical identity in 20000/20000 cases per arm
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Full current G9, dialect, higher-order relation or control-flow contexts expose surface-dependent semantic structure.
hypotheses.falsifier_next_test: Production parser full-corpus surface->typed-IR differential with identical semantic oracle.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Readable declared bare relations D remain viable only if the parser implements scoped soft-keyword/contextual declaration or explicit escaping that preserves the ordinary identifier namespace.
support: Finite resolver can reject unknown relation meaning
counterevidence: finite-terminal D proxy accepted 0/15 ordinary identifier controls using declared relation spellings
4B_emits and 4B_need_not_learn are not legal current identifiers
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: The namespace/escape machinery costs more complexity and repair burden than N or a lexically disjoint S.
hypotheses.falsifier_next_test: Production D parser passes full G9 plus identifier-shadowing/escape corpus with deterministic AST, zero accidental operator capture and acceptable diagnostics/latency.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A lexically disjoint sigil/custom surface could preserve compact readable relations while lowering to the same canonical IR.
support: bounded relation-only S proxy is compact and typed resolver fails unknown semantic IDs closed
counterevidence: concurrent mixed @ref test challenged current @relation spelling across LALR modes
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A redesigned disjoint sigil or quoted form removes the collision without losing compactness.
hypotheses.falsifier_next_test: Run redesigned S in the production parser against full G9+dialects and mixed ref/relation lexical stress corpus.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Strict normalization/generic relation form N is a robust canonical fallback for BASE parser closure.
support: concurrent whole-current-G9 proxy closed 86/86 chunks under N
this run found no identifier-namespace collision under N
counterevidence: relation sample cost averaged +12 bytes versus D
full migration edit count, diagnostics and target-reader repair cost are not yet matched against alternatives
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A softer custom surface yields equal correctness with materially lower reader/migration cost.
hypotheses.falsifier_next_test: Matched production N/S/D corpus benchmark including diagnostics, edits, token/context and Qwen-class reader repair.

hypotheses.hypothesis: BASE should freeze typed canonical IR semantics before freezing a preferred human/machine reader surface, provided every accepted surface roundtrips to the same semantic hash and authority/type invariants.
support: current N/S/D evidence converges on semantic admission being separate from surface recognition
independent MLIR architecture supports generic plus custom textual forms over one IR as an analogue
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Multiple source surfaces create unacceptable ambiguity, implementation complexity or migration burden and one strict source syntax should be frozen immediately.
hypotheses.falsifier_next_test: Production parser/canonicalizer benchmark plus target-reader study and compiler complexity measurement.
